c.tagline: The Mughals' marble masterpiece, crowned by the Taj Mahal.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws and cabs rarely use meters, so agree a fare first or book via Uber/Ola for a fixed price. Prepaid taxi booths operate at the airport and Agra Cantt railway station.

emergency.note: 112 is India's all-in-one emergency number; 108 reaches ambulance services and 101 is the fire brigade.

hood_landmark.Taj Ganj: Taj Ganj Taj Mahal south gate Agra

avoid.reason: Touts and commission scams around the Taj Mahal; overcharging and fake-guide hustles

hood_desc: The warren of narrow lanes hugging the Taj Mahal's south gate, packed with rooftop cafes framing the dome, marble-inlay workshops and cheap guesthouses; the closest and most atmospheric base for sunrise visits.

The planned hotel enclave by the Taj's quieter east gate, home to Agra's smartest resorts set among gardens minutes from the monument; ideal for travelers wanting comfort and Taj proximity without the old-town crush.
Agra's main tourist thoroughfare lined with mid-range and luxury hotels, restaurants and shops, roughly 2 km from all three Taj gates; convenient and well-serviced but busy and traffic-clogged.

The bustling commercial and shopping heart of Agra, famous for leather goods, handicrafts, sweets and street food around Sadar Bazaar; central for the Fort and city life, livelier and more local than the Taj hotels.
Agra's leafy colonial-era district along Mall Road, with heritage hotels, government offices and a calmer, greener feel; a quieter, more residential base a short ride from the main sights.
lodging: ITC Mughal, A Luxury Collection Resort & Spa

water.note: Drink only sealed bottled or filtered water.

transit.hours: Agra Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; shared autos and e-rickshaws operate from early morning until late evening.
transit.note: Agra Metro's first corridor (opened 2024) links key tourist stops including the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehabad Road. Beyond it, shared auto-rickshaws, cycle-rickshaws and battery e-rickshaws handle most short trips, with city buses on major routes.
transit.pay: Metro fares use tokens or a rechargeable smart card; autos and e-rickshaws are cash (or UPI/QR), with fares agreed before the ride.

air: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (DEL) ~230 km
train: Agra Cantt (AGC) - Gatimaan & Shatabdi Express from Delhi
Agra Fort & Raja ki Mandi stations

transit.m: Shared auto-rickshaw / local bus toward the city center (~40 min)
Prepaid taxi to the city center (30-40 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory, but rounding up or leaving ~10% at tourist restaurants is appreciated; guides and drivers expect a small tip.

food.name: Petha
food.desc: Translucent candied ash-gourd cubes, plain or flavoured with saffron, rose, paan or dry fruit; Agra's most famous edible souvenir.

places.name: Panchhi Petha
places.note: The name everyone in Agra names first; branches also on MG Road and in Sadar Bazaar.

places.name: Gopaldas Petha
places.note: Long-standing rival house known for softer angoori and kesar petha.

places.name: Bhimsain Jaju Petha
places.note: Old family shop claiming one of the original recipes; good dry-fruit versions.

food.name: Mughlai kebabs
food.desc: Seekh, boti and melt-in-the-mouth galouti kebabs cooked over charcoal, a direct inheritance from the Mughal court kitchens.

places.name: Peshawri
places.note: Signature grill room at ITC Mughal; tandoor-heavy menu and the famous dal.

places.name: Pinch of Spice
places.note: Reliably busy modern Mughlai kitchen popular with locals and visitors alike.

places.name: Mama Chicken Mama Franky House
places.note: Street-side legend for cheap, fast kebabs and rolls late into the evening.

food.name: Bedai with jalebi
food.desc: Agra's breakfast ritual: a puffed, spiced-lentil-stuffed fried bread served with peppery aloo sabzi and a hot coil of jalebi.

places.name: Deviram Sweets
places.note: Best-known sit-down address for the bedai-jalebi combination from early morning.

places.name: Bhagat Halwai
places.note: Old sweet house doing bedai, kachori and syrupy jalebi to a steady local crowd.

places.name: Rawatpara breakfast stalls
places.note: Cluster of early-morning bedai carts near Kinari Bazaar; go before 10am.

food.name: Dalmoth
food.desc: Dark, spicy Agra namkeen of fried lentils, nuts, curry leaves and raisins; the savoury counterweight to all that petha.

places.name: Hira Lal Dalmoth
places.note: The address most often cited for Agra's original dalmoth blend.

places.name: Panchhi Petha
places.note: Sells its own dalmoth and namkeen alongside the sweets.

places.name: Sadar Bazaar namkeen shops
places.note: Row of shops selling house blends by weight; ask for a taste before buying.

food.name: Mughlai curries
food.desc: Rich korma, nihari and creamy Mughlai chicken thickened with nuts and cream, still cooked to slow Mughal-era formulas.

places.name: Esphahan
places.note: Fine-dining room at The Oberoi Amarvilas with live Indian classical music.

places.name: Jahanpanah
places.note: Hotel Clarks Shiraz restaurant with a long-established Mughlai menu.

places.name: Pinch of Spice
places.note: Mid-priced favourite for korma, butter chicken and Mughlai gravies.

food.name: Agra chaat and bhalla
food.desc: Crisp fried lentil dumplings drowned in whipped yoghurt, tamarind and roasted cumin, plus aloo tikki and papdi chaat.

places.name: Seth Gali chaat lane
places.note: Narrow old-city lane where several generations-old chaat stalls sit side by side.

places.name: Sadar Bazaar chaat stalls
places.note: Evening chaat carts busiest around the pedestrian stretch.

places.name: Deviram Sweets
places.note: Clean sit-down option if you would rather not eat standing.

food.name: Masala chai
food.desc: Strong milky tea boiled with ginger, cardamom and clove, poured all day from kettles across the old city and Taj Ganj.

places.name: Sheroes Hangout
places.note: Cafe run by acid-attack survivors; pay what you like, and the chai is good.

places.name: Taj Ganj tea stalls
places.note: Cluster of kettle stalls on the walk between the south gate and the guesthouses.

places.name: Sadar Bazaar tea stalls
places.note: Busy evening chai carts alongside the snack shops.

food.name: Lassi and thandai
food.desc: Thick sweet or salted yoghurt lassi served in clay kulhads, plus chilled almond-and-spice thandai in the hot months.

places.name: Deviram Sweets
places.note: Kulhad lassi topped with cream, alongside the sweets counter.

places.name: Bhagat Halwai
places.note: Traditional halwai making lassi, rabri and seasonal thandai.

places.name: Kinari Bazaar lassi shops
places.note: Old-city stalls churning lassi by hand through the afternoon.

landmarks: Taj Mahal
Shah Jahan's ivory-marble mausoleum for empress Mumtaz Mahal, a UNESCO wonder whose dawn-lit dome and reflecting pools define eternal love in architecture.
Agra Fort
A colossal UNESCO-listed red sandstone citadel of the Mughal emperors, hiding pearl mosques, gilded palaces, and river views of the distant Taj.
Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
A jewel-box marble tomb sheathed in delicate pietra dura inlay, this refined 1620s mausoleum prefigured and inspired the Taj Mahal's design.
Mehtab Bagh
A Mughal charbagh garden directly across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal, offering photographers the classic sunset reflection view without the crowds.
Fatehpur Sikri
Emperor Akbar's abandoned red sandstone capital, a perfectly preserved UNESCO ghost city of palaces, courtyards, and the towering Buland Darwaza gateway.
Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
The great emperor's grand red sandstone and marble mausoleum, approached through gardens where blackbuck and langurs roam beneath inlaid gateways.
Jama Masjid
Agra's mighty 1648 Friday mosque built by Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara, its zigzag-patterned domes presiding over the frenetic old-city bazaars.
Chini Ka Rauza
The riverside tomb of Shah Jahan's poet-minister Afzal Khan, famed for its once-brilliant Persian glazed-tile facade glowing turquoise and orange.
Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)
Reputedly the oldest Mughal garden in India, laid out by Babur around 1528 as a Persian-style riverside retreat of terraces and pavilions.
Kinari Bazaar
A gloriously chaotic old-city market lane where marble inlay, glass bangles, wedding finery, and sizzling street snacks crowd every inch.

train.note: No international trains. Agra Cantt is the main station for Delhi, Jaipur and the south; Agra Fort station handles some eastern services. The Gatimaan Express covers Delhi to Agra in about 100 minutes and is the fastest way in, with the Taj Express and several Vande Bharat services alongside it. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead - day-trip trains from Delhi sell out well in advance.

bus.note: No international coaches. UPSRTC (https://www.upsrtc.up.gov.in/) buses run from Idgah and ISBT bus stands to Delhi, Jaipur, Mathura and Gwalior, with private Volvo coaches bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). The train is faster and more comfortable than the bus on the Delhi run.

ferry.note: Agra sits on the Yamuna but the river is not navigable for passenger services, so there are no ferries. Small boats sometimes offer river views of the Taj Mahal from the far bank as a photo excursion, not as transport.

half.name: Mathura and Vrindavan
half.blurb: Twin pilgrimage towns on the Yamuna River tied to Krishna's birth and childhood, filled with temples and devotional life.

half.name: Chand Baori (Abhaneri)
half.blurb: One of India's deepest stepwells, with thousands of symmetrical steps descending in a hypnotic geometric pattern.

full.name: Delhi
full.blurb: India's capital, with Mughal-era monuments like Humayun's Tomb and the Red Fort, a few hours north by road or rail.
